master_narrator.agency_handoff_prompt:
Isla didn't trust hard drives. They spun. They failed. They rusted. Crystals were forever.

She sat in the center of the Simulacrum, the holographic projector humming around her in the quiet subterranean dark. Orbiting droplets of liquid iron danced in the air, a bioluminescent wonder choreographed to a minor-key cello chord. It was a flawless demonstration of magneto-acoustic cymatics coupling polyphonic synthesizer harmonics into an electromagnet matrix, suspending ferrofluid droplets in gravity-defying resonant spires. Yet, despite encoding terabytes per second of five-dimensional holographic storm telemetry into nanostructured quartz, she still found herself hand-polishing the primary optical lenses with a scrap of chamois leather until her fingers cramped. 

A sudden, sharp fluctuation in the local magnetic field tore through the chamber. The minor-key cello chord stuttered into a dissonant shriek, and the ferrofluid spires began to destabilize, threatening to splash their highly corrosive mass across the delicate quartz lattice. Isla's heart hammered. A cautious archivist would initiate a safe shutdown, preserving the hardware at the cost of the incoming data stream. But as the structural integrity alarms blared, her Sagittarius override kicked in. The cautious architect vanished, replaced by a reckless gambler betting the entire optical array on a single, untested pulse of inverted polarity.

She slammed her hand against the synthesizer, forcing a raw, overpowering chord into the matrix. The droplets froze in mid-air, trembling violently before snapping back into perfect, impossible alignment. She let out a long breath, her hands shaking slightly as she rubbed her cramped fingers against the chamois. 

'If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong,' a voice echoed from the doorway. Dorian stepped into the soft glow, his eyes tracking the stabilized iron droplets with quiet appreciation. He carried his own slate, ready for his shift. 

'I wasn't complaining,' Isla replied dryly, standing up and passing him the heavy brass calibration ledger. 'I was simply pointing out the persistent inefficiency of physical reality. The lattice is holding, but the pulse requires constant monitoring.' Dorian took the baton handoff with a nod, stepping into the center of the humming matrix as Isla moved toward the door, leaving him to the quiet company of dancing iron.
